subject.name: rev_print
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string and displays it reversed, followed
by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./rev_print "hello" | cat -e
olleh$
$> ./rev_print "a" | cat -e
a$
$> ./rev_print | cat -e
$
$> ./rev_print "ab" "cd" | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: maff_alpha
subject.description:
Write a program that displays the alphabet in lowercase, on a single
line, in ascending order, followed by a newline.
Parameters, if any, are ignored.

subject.name: maff_revalpha
subject.description:
Write a program that displays the alphabet in lowercase, on a single
line, in descending order, followed by a newline.
Parameters, if any, are ignored.

subject.name: write_string
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
it as-is, followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: odd
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one integer as a parameter.
If that number is odd, display `Odd number` followed by a newline.
In any other case (even number, wrong number of parameters), display
nothing at all.
subject.examples:
$> ./odd "3" | cat -e
Odd number$
$> ./odd "4" | cat -e
$
$> ./odd "-7" | cat -e
Odd number$
$> ./odd "0" | cat -e
$
$> ./odd | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: even
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one integer as a parameter.
If that number is even, display `Even number` followed by a newline.
In any other case (odd number, wrong number of parameters), display
nothing at all.
subject.examples:
$> ./even "4" | cat -e
Even number$
$> ./even "3" | cat -e
$
$> ./even "0" | cat -e
Even number$
$> ./even "-2" | cat -e
Even number$
$> ./even | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: interval_space
subject.description:
Write a program that takes two integers as parameters and displays
every integer from the first to the second (inclusive), separated by a
single space, followed by a newline.
If the first integer is greater than the second, or the number of
parameters is not 2, simply display a newline.

subject.name: occ_a
subject.description:
Write a program that counts how many times the character `a` (lowercase)
appears across all its parameters, then displays the total as a number
followed by a newline.
If there are no parameters, display `0`.

subject.name: occ_z
subject.description:
Write a program that counts how many times the character `z` (lowercase)
appears across all its parameters, then displays the total as a number
followed by a newline.
If there are no parameters, display `0`.

subject.name: count_len
subject.description:
Write a program that displays the total number of characters across all
of its parameters (not counting spaces between them), followed by a
newline.
If there are no parameters, display `0`.

subject.name: count_alen
subject.description:
Write a program that displays the total number of alphabetic characters
(`a`-`z`, `A`-`Z`) across all of its parameters, followed by a newline.
If there are no parameters, display `0`.

subject.name: nth_char
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string and an index N as parameters, then
displays the character at index N in the string, followed by a newline.
If N is out of bounds, or the number of parameters is not 2, simply
display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./nth_char "hello" "1" | cat -e
e$
$> ./nth_char "hello" "0" | cat -e
h$
$> ./nth_char "hello" "10" | cat -e
$
$> ./nth_char "hello" "-1" | cat -e
$
$> ./nth_char | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: rle
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string and displays it encoded using Run-Length
Encoding, followed by a newline.
Run-Length Encoding replaces each maximal sequence of identical consecutive
characters (a "run") with the number of characters in the run followed by the
character itself. A run cannot exceed 9 characters: if more than 9 identical
characters follow each other, split them into multiple chunks of at most 9.
If a run (or chunk) has only 1 character, display the character alone,
without the count.
If the number of parameters is not 1, or if the string is empty, simply
display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./rle "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabbbvfe" | cat -e
9a9a3a3bvfe$
$> ./rle "aabbbbcccccccccccccc" | cat -e
2a4b9c5c$
$> ./rle "" | cat -e
$
$> ./rle "a" "b" | cat -e
$
$> ./rle "hello" | cat -e
he2lo$
$>

subject.name: digit_sum
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one integer as a parameter and displays the
sum of its decimal digits, followed by a newline (the sign is ignored).
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: first_last_char
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
its first and last character concatenated, followed by a newline.
If the string has only one character, display it once.
If the string is empty, or the number of parameters is not 1, simply
display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./first_last_char "hello" | cat -e
ho$
$> ./first_last_char "a" | cat -e
a$
$> ./first_last_char "ab" | cat -e
ab$
$> ./first_last_char | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: count_letters
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
the number of alphabetic characters (`a`-`z`, `A`-`Z`) it contains,
followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: pingpong
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one integer N as a parameter. For every
integer `i` from 1 to N: if `i` is a multiple of 2 and 3, display
`pingpong`; else if `i` is a multiple of 2, display `ping`; else if `i`
is a multiple of 3, display `pong`; otherwise display `i` itself. Values
are separated by a single space, and the whole line ends with a newline.
If N is less than 1, or the number of parameters is not 1, simply
display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./pingpong "15" | cat -e
1 ping pong ping 5 pingpong 7 ping pong ping 11 pingpong 13 ping pong$
$> ./pingpong "1" | cat -e
1$
$> ./pingpong "6" | cat -e
1 ping pong ping 5 pingpong$
$> ./pingpong "0" | cat -e
$
$> ./pingpong | cat -e
$
$>

testCases.expected: 1 ping pong ping 5 pingpong 7 ping pong ping 11 pingpong 13 ping pong

subject.name: aff_first_param
subject.description:
Write a program that displays its first parameter followed by a
newline.
If there are no parameters, simply display a newline.

subject.name: aff_last_param
subject.description:
Write a program that displays its last parameter followed by a
newline.
If there are no parameters, simply display a newline.

subject.name: last_word
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string (a sentence, quote it if it
contains spaces) as its only parameter and displays its last word
(words are separated by one or more spaces), followed by a newline.
If there is no word (empty string, only spaces), or the number of
parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./last_word "hello world foo" | cat -e
foo$
$> ./last_word "  a  b  " | cat -e
b$
$> ./last_word "   " | cat -e
$
$> ./last_word | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: union
subject.description:
Write a program that takes two strings as parameters and displays every
distinct character that appears in either string, each once, in order
of first appearance (scanning the first string then the second),
followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 2, simply display a newline.

subject.name: inter
subject.description:
Write a program that takes two strings as parameters and displays every
distinct character that appears in both strings, each once, in order
of first appearance in the first string, followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 2, simply display a newline.

subject.name: wdmatch
subject.description:
Write a program that takes two strings as parameters and displays `1`
followed by a newline if the first string is a subsequence of the
second (its characters appear in the second string in the same order,
not necessarily contiguous), otherwise displays `0` followed by a
newline.
If the number of parameters is not 2, simply display a newline.

subject.name: is_palindrome
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
`1` followed by a newline if it reads the same forwards and backwards
(case-sensitive, character by character), otherwise displays `0`
followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: title
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
it in Title Case: the first letter of every word capitalized, every
other letter lowercased, and any non-letter character left untouched.
A new word starts at the beginning of the string and right after any
non-alphabetic character. The result is followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./title "hello world" | cat -e
Hello World$
$> ./title "MULTIPLE   SPACES here" | cat -e
Multiple   Spaces Here$
$> ./title | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: search_and_replace
subject.description:
Write a program that takes three strings as parameters: a haystack, a
needle, and a replacement. It displays the haystack with every
non-overlapping occurrence of the needle replaced by the replacement,
followed by a newline. If the needle is empty, the haystack is
displayed unchanged.
If the number of parameters is not 3, simply display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./search_and_replace "hello world hello" "hello" "hi" | cat -e
hi world hi$
$> ./search_and_replace "aaa" "aa" "b" | cat -e
ba$
$> ./search_and_replace "abc" "x" "y" | cat -e
abc$
$> ./search_and_replace | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: base16
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
it encoded in base16 (hexadecimal): each byte becomes two uppercase hex
digits, concatenated with no separator, followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

ft_split.name: ft_split

subject.name: ft_split
subject.description:
Split the string `s` into an array of strings, using `c` as a
delimiter. Consecutive delimiters do not produce empty strings.
Return a `NULL`-terminated, malloc'd array of malloc'd strings.
notes: Do not include a `main` in your file — the grader links its own.
Every string in the array (and the array itself) must be freeable.

ft_list_remove_if.name: ft_list_remove_if

subject.name: ft_list_remove_if
subject.description:
Given a singly-linked list of `int` (see `t_list` below) and a value,
remove every node whose `value` matches from the list, freeing each
removed node.
A `t_list.h` header defining the list type is provided automatically —
add `#include "t_list.h"` at the top of your file to use it.

sort_list.name: sort_list

subject.name: sort_list
subject.description:
Given a singly-linked list of `int` (see `t_list` below), sort it in
place in ascending order by swapping node `value`s (do not reallocate
or relink nodes).
A `t_list.h` header defining the list type is provided automatically —
add `#include "t_list.h"` at the top of your file to use it.

subject.name: count_alpha
subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string as its only parameter and displays
the number of alphabetic characters (`a`-`z`, `A`-`Z`) it contains,
followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: ord_alphlong
subject.description:
Write a program that takes several strings as parameters and displays
them, space-separated, sorted by their number of alphabetic characters
in descending order (ties keep their original relative order),
followed by a newline.
If there are no parameters, simply display a newline.
subject.examples:
$> ./ord_alphlong "ab" "abc" "a" | cat -e
abc ab a$
$> ./ord_alphlong "x" "abcdef" "yz" | cat -e
abcdef yz x$
$> ./ord_alphlong | cat -e
$
$>

subject.name: str_maxlenoc
subject.description:
Write a program that takes several strings as parameters. Find the
first string with the maximum length, then count how many parameters
are exactly equal to it. Display that string, a single space, and the
count, followed by a newline.
If there are no parameters, simply display a newline.

subject.name: count_island
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one parameter: a grid where rows are
separated by commas and cells are `1` (land) or `0` (water). Display
the number of islands, where an island is a group of `1`s connected
horizontally or vertically (not diagonally), followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: g_diam
subject.description:
Write a program that takes one parameter describing an undirected,
unweighted graph: edges separated by commas, each edge written as
`a-b` where `a` and `b` are node ids (non-negative integers). Display
the graph's diameter — the longest shortest path between any two
nodes that are connected to each other — followed by a newline.
If the number of parameters is not 1, simply display a newline.

subject.name: infin_mult
subject.description:
Write a program that takes two non-negative integers as strings
(arbitrarily large — too big to fit in any native integer type) and
displays their product as a decimal string, followed by a newline, with
no leading zeros (except the result `0` itself).
If the number of parameters is not 2, simply display a newline.
